title: Row-minor ideals of submodules: stabilization and coordinate invariance
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $n,k\ge0$. For an $R$-submodule $K\subseteq R^{\oplus n}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], put $D_k(K;n)=R$ if $n\le k$; otherwise let $D_k(K;n)$ be the ideal generated by the determinants [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of all $(n-k)\times(n-k)$ submatrices [def-weil-submatrix] of all $(n-k)\times n$ matrices [def-weil-matrix] whose rows lie in $K$. Use the same definition for every finite ambient rank. Then:
(1) For $n>k$, $D_k(K;n)$ is the sum of $J_{n-k}(A)$ over all finite matrices $A$ with $n$ columns and rows in $K$, where $J_r$ is [def-trf-minor-ideal].
(2) For every $d\ge0$, $D_k(K\oplus R^{\oplus d};n+d)=D_k(K;n)$, with $K\oplus R^{\oplus d}$ embedded by the first $n$ and last $d$ coordinates.
(3) For every $R$-linear automorphism $u:R^{\oplus n}\to R^{\oplus n}$, $D_k(u(K);n)=D_k(K;n)$.
No finite generation of $K$ is assumed.

proof.text: Put $r=n-k>0$. By [def-trf-minor-ideal], each generator of $J_r(A)$ is obtained by selecting $r$ rows of $A$ and $r$ columns. Those selected rows lie in $K$, so it is a generator of $D_k(K;n)$. Conversely each generator of $D_k(K;n)$ belongs to $J_r(A)$ for its defining $r\times n$ row matrix $A$. The two generated ideals coincide, proving (1), without requiring one finite matrix to contain all of $K$.

For (2), first suppose $n\le k$. If $n+d\le k$, both ideals are $R$ by definition. Otherwise $s=n+d-k$ satisfies $1\le s\le d$. Choose $s$ standard basis rows and the same $s$ columns among the last $d$ coordinates of $K\oplus R^{\oplus d}$. Their minor is $I_s$, of determinant $1$: in the formula of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] only the identity permutation contributes. Hence the enlarged ideal contains $1$ and also equals $R$.

source.place: Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), zero-generator stabilization paragraph; cutoff cases made explicit

proof.text: Now suppose $n>k$ and put $r=n-k$. Given a defining row matrix $A$ for $D_k(K;n)$, append $d$ zero columns, then the $d$ standard basis rows on these columns. The resulting $(r+d)\times(n+d)$ matrix has rows in $K\oplus R^{\oplus d}$. Each old minor $Q$, together with the last $d$ rows and columns, gives $\operatorname{diag}(Q,I_d)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-block-triangular-determinant] its determinant is $\det(Q)\det(I_d)=\det(Q)$; the identity determinant is $1$ by [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Thus every old generator belongs to the enlarged ideal.

source.place: Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), zero-generator stabilization paragraph, first inclusion

proof.text: Conversely, let $B$ be any defining $(r+d)\times(n+d)$ row matrix in $K\oplus R^{\oplus d}$ and let $A$ be its first $n$ columns. All rows of $A$ lie in $K$. Part (2) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-minor-inclusions] gives $J_{r+d}(B)\subseteq J_r(A)$, and step 1 gives $J_r(A)\subseteq D_k(K;n)$. This places every enlarged generator in the old ideal and completes (2).

source.place: Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), zero-generator stabilization paragraph, converse using Tag 07Z7(2)

proof.text: For (3), the case $n\le k$ is definitional. Otherwise set $r=n-k$ and $C_{ij}=u(e_i)_j$. Linearity gives $u(z)_j=\sum_i z_i C_{ij}$. Consequently any defining row matrix in $u(K)$ is $AC$ for a matrix $A$ whose rows are the inverse images in $K$. Part (3) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-minor-inclusions] gives $J_r(AC)\subseteq J_r(A)\subseteq D_k(K;n)$ by step 1. Thus $D_k(u(K);n)\subseteq D_k(K;n)$. Apply this same inclusion to $u^{-1}$ and $u(K)$ to obtain the reverse inclusion.

lean.statement: theorem rowMinorIdeal_stable_invariance {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (n k : ℕ) (K : Submodule R (Fin n → R)) : (k < n → rowMinorIdeal n k K = ⨆ (p : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin n) R) (_ : ∀ i : Fin p, A i ∈ K), minorIdeal p n (n - k) A) ∧ (∀ d : ℕ, rowMinorIdeal (n + d) k (K.comap (LinearMap.pi fun j : Fin n ↦ (LinearMap.proj (Fin.castAdd d j) : (Fin (n + d) → R) →ₗ[R] R))) = rowMinorIdeal n k K) ∧ (∀ u : (Fin n → R) ≃ₗ[R] (Fin n → R), rowMinorIdeal n k (K.map u.toLinearMap) = rowMinorIdeal n k K)
lean.note: The module also supplies the row-minor ideal D_k(K;n) introduced in this node itself, as Matrix.rowMinorIdeal. Its real data is the supremum of Matrix.minorIdeal over all defining (n-k)-row matrices, with the explicit n <= k cutoff. No independent notion or dependency is redefined.

reviewed_lean.note: The node changes only in lean; lean.statement is verbatim in the file. rowMinorIdeal is the whole ring for n≤k, else the supremum of minorIdeal (n-k) n (n-k) A over matrices with rows in K, i.e. exactly D_k(K;n). Clause (1) holds under k<n as a supremum over all p and Fin p-row matrices. Clause (2): the comap along the first-n projections (Fin.castAdd) is K⊕R^d, at rank n+d with the same k. Clause (3): every linear equivalence u, image K.map u. No extra hypotheses; universe bound. Edge cases n=0, d=0, k=0, n≤k<n+d, K=0/K=everything, zero ring are covered. One sorry; docstrings carry source, blueprint id and 5 proof steps; report has both sections. Not recompiled (no file changed). Advisory: the parent's presentationFittingIdeal is the same ideal for ker π; reuse here would close an import cycle, so the parent's stage-3 proof needs a bridge lemma. The FreeModule.Basic import is unused (H9, redundant).
